trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cancun
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Playa Delfines Beach Day
experiences.description: Visit one of Cancun's most iconic and uncrowded public beaches. Playa Delfines offers stunning turquoise waters, white sand, and the famous Cancun sign for photos. No entry fee and less crowded than hotel zone beaches, perfect for swimming and relaxing.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on Flight AA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange budget-friendly airport transfer to Cancun Beach Resort (shared shuttle recommended, ~$10-15 USD vs expensive taxis). Check in or drop bags if room isn't ready.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a short walk to the nearest public beach access point near the hotel. Relax on the beach, swim in the Caribbean Sea, and get oriented with your surroundings. Grab a cold drink from a local beach vendor to kick off the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Hotel Zone (Zona Hotelera) boulevard to explore the area. Find a casual local restaurant or taco stand for a relaxed first dinner. Head back to the resort early to rest after travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light meal at the airport before or after landing — look for local bakery options or a convenience store near arrivals to keep costs low (~$3-5 USD).
meals.lunch: Pick up affordable street tacos or visit a local cocina económica near the hotel for a filling meal (~$5-8 USD).
meals.dinner: Try La Parrilla or a similar mid-range Mexican restaurant in the Zona Hotelera for authentic cuisine at reasonable prices (~$10-15 USD). Look for early-bird specials.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light since you're arriving midday and may be jet-lagged. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. Exchange some currency to Mexican Pesos at the airport or a local bank for better rates than hotel exchange desks. Avoid tourist trap restaurants right at the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day early with a visit to Playa Delfines, one of Cancun's most iconic and uncrowded public beaches. Take the R-1 public bus from the Hotel Zone (only ~$0.80 USD) heading south to reach this stunning turquoise beach. Arrive early to claim a good spot before crowds build. Swim, relax, and enjoy panoramic views of the Caribbean Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Playa Delfines through the early afternoon. Explore the beach, take photos at the famous 'CANCUN' sign, and wade in the crystal-clear water. Pack a light snack or buy from a beach vendor to save money. Head back toward the hotel zone by bus in the mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Mercado 28 area or a local neighborhood market for souvenir shopping and people-watching. Enjoy a casual dinner at a neighborhood restaurant away from the main tourist strip for better prices.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel if breakfast is included, or visit a nearby panadería (bakery) for fresh pastries and coffee (~$2-4 USD).
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches or snacks from a local convenience store (OXXO) before heading to Playa Delfines to save money (~$3-5 USD). Alternatively, buy from beach vendors (~$5-7 USD).
meals.dinner: Head to El Mercado 28 food court for authentic, affordable Mexican dishes like enchiladas, tamales, or pozole (~$6-10 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is a free public beach — no entry fee. Bring sunscreen, a reusable water bottle, and a beach towel from the hotel. The R-1 bus runs frequently along Kukulcan Boulevard and is by far the cheapest way to get around the Hotel Zone. Avoid renting beach chairs from vendors if budget is tight — the public beach area is free to use.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full-day trip to Dos Ojos Cenotes, one of the most spectacular freshwater cave systems near Cancun. Book a budget group tour in advance (~$40-60 USD including transport and snorkel gear) or arrange a shared colectivo van to Tulum direction and get dropped near the site. Arrive early to beat the crowds and enjoy the crystal-clear cenote waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Dos Ojos — there are two main cenotes (the 'Bat Cave' and the 'Barbie Line') to snorkel through. The underwater visibility is extraordinary. Take your time floating through the cave systems and admiring stalactites and stalagmites. Enjoy lunch at the cenote's small on-site café or bring your own packed lunch to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by late afternoon. Rest at the hotel and freshen up. Spend a low-key evening walking the beach near the resort at sunset — one of the most beautiful and completely free experiences Cancun offers.

meals.breakfast: Eat a hearty breakfast before departure — hotel breakfast if available, or a filling meal at a local comedor (~$4-6 USD) to fuel the day's adventure.
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch (sandwiches, fruit, snacks from OXXO) to bring to Dos Ojos to avoid overpriced on-site food. Budget ~$3-5 USD.
meals.dinner: Try Taquería Los Arcos or a similar local taco spot back in Cancun for an affordable and delicious dinner (~$6-9 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Dos Ojos tour in advance online for the best group rates. Bring water shoes if you have them, as some surfaces can be slippery. A waterproof phone case or dry bag is highly recommended. Life jackets are usually provided. Dos Ojos is about 1.5 hours from Cancun — plan for an early start (depart by 8:00 AM). No sunscreen allowed in the cenotes to protect the ecosystem — bring biodegradable alternatives or rinse off before entering.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed morning at Playa Tortugas or Playa Caracol, two free public beaches in the northern Hotel Zone that are easily accessible from the resort. These beaches are calmer and great for swimming. Arrive early for the best experience before the midday heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the bus to explore the free sections of the Hotel Zone. Visit the Mayan Museum of Cancun (El Museo Maya de Cancún) — entrance is very affordable (~$4-5 USD) and includes access to the adjacent San Miguelito archaeological ruins. This is a great budget-friendly cultural activity with fascinating history.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Parque de las Palapas in Downtown Cancun (El Centro) via public bus. This lively local square often has free live music, street performers, and a fantastic night market atmosphere. Enjoy cheap local street food and mingle with locals.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a local café or hotel — try chilaquiles or huevos rancheros at a nearby comedor (~$3-5 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat near the museum area — look for a local lunch spot serving a 'comida corrida' (set lunch menu with soup, main, and drink) for excellent value (~$5-8 USD).
meals.dinner: Feast on street food at Parque de las Palapas — elotes (grilled corn), tacos, gorditas, and fresh fruit cups are all available for very little money (~$4-7 USD total).

day_by_day.notes: The Mayan Museum is closed on Mondays, so Thursday is perfect. Downtown Cancun (El Centro) is much cheaper than the Hotel Zone for food and shopping. The public bus to El Centro costs less than $1 USD. Parque de las Palapas is safest and most lively in the evening — it's a favorite among locals and a great authentic experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to Isla Mujeres via the public ferry from Puerto Juárez (not the more expensive hotel zone ferry). The round-trip ferry costs approximately $8-10 USD. Arrive on the island early and rent a golf cart (~$40-50 USD split between travel companions) or explore on foot to keep costs low.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Playa Norte on Isla Mujeres — consistently rated one of the most beautiful beaches in the Caribbean with calm, shallow turquoise water. Swim, snorkel, and relax. Explore the colorful streets of the island village, browse local craft shops, and visit the free cliff viewpoint at the southern tip of the island.
day_by_day.evening: Return on the ferry to Cancun by late afternoon/early evening. Enjoy a final sunset beach walk near the hotel. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner to celebrate a wonderful trip — look for happy hour deals at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before heading to the ferry — grab a torta or tamale from a street vendor near Puerto Juárez (~$2-3 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat fresh seafood on Isla Mujeres — fish tacos and ceviche from local restaurants near Playa Norte are affordable and delicious (~$8-12 USD).
meals.dinner: Back in Cancun, try a restaurant with a happy hour deal — many Hotel Zone spots offer 2-for-1 drinks and discounted food between 5-7 PM (~$10-15 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Take the public ferry from Puerto Juárez (north of Hotel Zone) — it's significantly cheaper than the tourist ferries from the Hotel Zone docks. The bus to Puerto Juárez from the Hotel Zone costs under $1 USD. Isla Mujeres is very walkable but a golf cart makes it easier — split the cost with other travelers if possible. Bring cash as some small island vendors don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cancun — wake up early for one last sunrise beach walk. Take a final dip in the Caribbean Sea and soak in the beautiful views. Pack your bags and check out of the hotel. Store luggage at the front desk if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your last few hours exploring a nearby local market for any last-minute souvenir shopping. Visit Mercado 23 in El Centro for the most authentic and cheapest souvenirs (avoid hotel zone shops which are heavily marked up). Head to the airport with plenty of time — allow at least 2.5-3 hours before departure for international flights.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cancun International Airport. Enjoy one final taco or snack at the airport before boarding. Reflect on an amazing budget-friendly Cancun adventure!

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast if included, or grab fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee at a local café near the hotel (~$3-5 USD).
meals.lunch: Quick and affordable lunch at Mercado 23 food stalls in El Centro — try a comida corrida for a filling last meal (~$5-7 USD).
meals.dinner: Airport food or a light snack before departure — budget ~$5-10 USD. Alternatively, eat a bigger lunch and just grab a snack at the airport.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is usually 12:00 PM — confirm with the hotel. The shared airport shuttle back to the airport is the most budget-friendly option (~$10-15 USD). Mercado 23 is a local favorite and far cheaper than tourist markets — great for vanilla, hot sauces, and handicrafts. Declare any food items at customs when returning home. Keep some pesos for tips and last-minute expenses.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on flight AA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Cancun Beach Resort in the Hotel Zone. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the resort amenities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the resort beach or pool to relax and decompress after travel. Take a leisurely stroll along the Hotel Zone (Zona Hotelera) boulevard to get your bearings, pick up essentials at a nearby convenience store or pharmacy, and soak in your first views of the Caribbean Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a welcome dinner at a mid-range restaurant near the Hotel Zone. Try La Habichuela Downtown or a local seafood spot like El Fish Fritanga for fresh ceviche and grilled fish to kick off the trip right.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing
meals.lunch: Light bite at the resort restaurant or a casual beachside taco stand near the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: El Fish Fritanga or La Parrilla Cancun — budget around $15–25 USD per person for fresh seafood and Mexican classics

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 11:00 AM, keep Day 1 low-key. Allow 45–60 minutes for customs and baggage claim, plus 30–45 minutes for the transfer to the Hotel Zone. Don't overplan — rest is key for enjoying the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with breakfast at the resort, then head out for a full Playa Delfines Beach Day. Visit one of Cancun's most iconic and uncrowded public beaches. Playa Delfines offers stunning turquoise waters and a more local, relaxed atmosphere compared to busier Hotel Zone beaches. Arrive early (by 9:00–9:30 AM) to claim a great spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Playa Delfines through the early afternoon — swim, sunbathe, and take photos at the famous 'CANCUN' sign landmark. Around 2:00 PM, head back toward the Hotel Zone and stop at a beachside palapa restaurant for a long, leisurely lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Mercado 28 (Market 28) area for some souvenir shopping and local color, then enjoy dinner at a traditional Mexican restaurant nearby. End the evening with a walk along the Hotel Zone strip or a drink at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or a local café — budget $8–12 USD
meals.lunch: Beachside palapa restaurant near Playa Delfines such as El Oasis — fresh fish tacos and agua fresca for $10–18 USD
meals.dinner: La Parrilla Cancun in the Hotel Zone — authentic Mexican cuisine with mariachi music, $20–30 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is accessible via the R-1 public bus along Kukulcan Boulevard — very affordable at about 12 MXN (~$0.60 USD). Bring sunscreen, a beach umbrella if possible, and plenty of water. There are no beach clubs here, so it's a bring-your-own setup.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Isla Mujeres Catamaran Tour — one of the top experiences near Cancun. Depart from the Hotel Zone marina around 9:00–9:30 AM. Enjoy snorkeling in crystal-clear Caribbean waters, spot colorful fish and coral reefs, and sail toward the charming island of Isla Mujeres.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Isla Mujeres and explore the island's colorful streets, boutique shops, and white-sand beaches. Visit Playa Norte, consistently ranked among the best beaches in Mexico. Enjoy lunch on the island at a local restaurant. Return catamaran typically departs around 3:00–4:00 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening, shower, and relax. Enjoy a sunset cocktail at the resort bar or a nearby rooftop. Have a lighter dinner close to the hotel to recover from a full day on the water.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — $8–12 USD or included with stay
meals.lunch: Lunch on Isla Mujeres at Mango Cafe or Sunset Grill — fresh grilled fish, lobster, or ceviche for $15–25 USD
meals.dinner: Casual dinner near the resort such as Contramar or a Hotel Zone sushi/fusion spot — $18–28 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: The Isla Mujeres Catamaran Tour typically costs $55–85 USD per person and includes snorkeling gear, open bar, and sometimes lunch. Book at least one day in advance. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a light rash guard, and a waterproof bag for your phone and valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Swim in the Cenotes at Dos Ojos. Depart early (around 8:00–8:30 AM) for the drive south toward Tulum — approximately 1.5 to 2 hours from Cancun. Dos Ojos is a famous freshwater cave system featuring crystal-clear underground cenotes. Explore the caverns, swim in the ethereal blue water, and snorkel through the cave passages.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cenote experience, stop in the Tulum area for a late lunch at one of the trendy beachside or jungle restaurants. Optionally, make a brief stop at the Tulum archaeological ruins (Zona Arqueológica) for panoramic views of the Caribbean — entrance fee is modest at around $5–7 USD. Begin the drive back to Cancun by 4:00–4:30 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Cancun by early evening. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed dinner in the Hotel Zone. Consider a beachside restaurant with ambient lighting for a memorable evening.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast at the resort or pack snacks for the road — $6–10 USD
meals.lunch: Lunch near Tulum at a mid-range spot like Burrito Amor or a local cocina — $12–20 USD
meals.dinner: Harry's Prime Steakhouse & Raw Bar or Puerto Madero in the Hotel Zone for a slightly elevated mid-range dinner — $25–40 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Dos Ojos cenote entry costs approximately $18–25 USD per person. Snorkel gear rental is available on-site for $5–10 USD. Renting a car for this day trip is the most flexible option ($40–60 USD/day) or join an organized tour ($50–80 USD). No sunscreen allowed in the cenotes — biodegradable alternatives are recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at the Playa Tortugas Beach Club Experience. Head to Playa Tortugas, a lively public beach in the Hotel Zone with access to beach clubs. Arrive by 9:30–10:00 AM to secure a good spot. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere, water sports rentals (jet skis, paddleboards), and the beautiful beach setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at Playa Tortugas or transition to the beach club pool area. Many beach clubs offer day passes ($20–40 USD) that include a credit toward food and drinks. Enjoy the social atmosphere, try water activities, and relax under a palapa.
day_by_day.evening: Cap off the evening with the Sunset Cruise along the Caribbean Coast. Board a sunset sailing cruise departing from the Hotel Zone lagoon. Enjoy stunning golden-hour views of the Caribbean, sip cocktails, and watch the sky transform into brilliant oranges and pinks. Cruises typically run 2–2.5 hours.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort or a local café — $8–12 USD
meals.lunch: Lunch at the beach club at Playa Tortugas — nachos, ceviche, burgers, or seafood with drinks included in the day pass credit — $15–25 USD
meals.dinner: Light dinner after the sunset cruise at a casual Hotel Zone spot or resort restaurant — $15–22 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: The Sunset Cruise typically costs $45–70 USD per person and often includes an open bar and light snacks. Book in advance, especially on a Friday. Combine the beach club day with the evening cruise for a perfect full-day beach experience. Playa Tortugas is easily accessible via the R-1 bus.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cancun — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort and take one last swim in the Caribbean Sea from the resort beach. Pack up, check out, and store luggage with the concierge if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the last afternoon doing any remaining shopping at La Isla Shopping Mall (open-air mall in the Hotel Zone with great views and mid-range shops) or revisit a favorite beach spot. Pick up local gifts, hot sauces, vanilla, or artisan crafts. Head to the airport with ample time — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for international flights.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cancun International Airport. Enjoy a final meal or snack at the airport before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — enjoy it fully as a send-off meal, $10–15 USD or included
meals.lunch: La Isla Shopping Mall food court or a nearby casual restaurant for a final Mexican meal — $12–20 USD
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a pre-departure meal at a restaurant near the airport — $15–25 USD

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically 11:00 AM — ask the resort about late check-out if needed (may incur a fee). Cancun airport is about 15–20 minutes from the Hotel Zone. Keep some cash in Mexican pesos for last-minute tips, taxis, or small purchases. Exchange or spend remaining pesos before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on Flight AA. A private luxury transfer will be arranged to whisk you directly to the Cancun Beach Resort. Check-in, unpack, and settle into your premium suite overlooking the Caribbean Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: After freshening up, take a leisurely first look at the resort's private beach. Enjoy a welcome cocktail by the pool or shore, and soak in the turquoise waters of the Hotel Zone. This is a relaxed orientation afternoon — no structured tours, just pure arrival bliss.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Cruise along the Caribbean Coast — Board a private or small-group sunset sailing cruise departing from the Hotel Zone lagoon. Enjoy golden-hour panoramas of the Caribbean, champagne on deck, and light canapés as the sky turns amber and rose.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a light breakfast or brunch at the resort's signature restaurant upon arrival — try fresh tropical fruit, avocado toast, and freshly squeezed juices to kick off the trip.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the resort's beachfront restaurant — indulge in ceviche, grilled shrimp tacos, and a chilled margarita while taking in your first views of the Hotel Zone shoreline.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Fisheria (Cancun Hotel Zone) — a premium seafood restaurant celebrated for its fresh catches, creative cocktails, and upscale ambiance. Reserve a window table for lingering harbor views.

day_by_day.notes: Given the 11:00 AM arrival, allow 60–90 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and the private transfer to the resort. Pre-arrange your luxury transfer in advance to avoid any delays. Confirm sunset cruise timing with the concierge upon check-in — most depart around 5:00–6:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Playa Delfines Beach Day — Start your morning with a visit to Playa Delfines, one of Cancun's most iconic and uncrowded public beaches. Arrive early to claim the best spot and enjoy the dramatic turquoise-and-emerald Caribbean waters with a backdrop of ancient dunes. Bring a premium beach bag, SPF, and a good book.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your Playa Delfines experience through the early afternoon, then return to the resort for a pampering session at the resort spa. Book a 90-minute deep tissue or hot stone massage to ease any travel fatigue and fully settle into vacation mode.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Hotel Zone's Kukulcan Boulevard at dusk, browsing luxury boutiques and art galleries. Then head to dinner at a rooftop restaurant for a sophisticated evening under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — a full à la carte spread featuring eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, tropical fruit platters, and artisan coffee or fresh-pressed juice.
meals.lunch: Pack a premium picnic from the resort's deli or stop at a beachside palapa near Playa Delfines for freshly made guacamole, shrimp cocktail, and agua fresca.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Porfirio's Cancun (Hotel Zone) — an iconic upscale Mexican restaurant with a vibrant atmosphere, live music, and an exceptional menu of traditional Mexican cuisine elevated with premium ingredients. Don't miss the tableside guacamole and mezcal cocktails.

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is a public beach with no private beach clubs, so bring your own premium beach gear (umbrella, towels, cooler). It is best visited in the morning before crowds and heat peak. Taxis and hotel shuttles can reach it easily from the Hotel Zone.

day_by_day.morning: Isla Mujeres Catamaran Tour — Depart from the Hotel Zone marina on a luxury catamaran bound for the stunning island of Isla Mujeres. Enjoy snorkeling in crystal-clear Caribbean waters teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral. Opt for a private charter for an exclusive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive on Isla Mujeres and explore the colorful, charming streets of the island town. Visit Punta Sur (the southernmost tip of Mexico) for dramatic cliff views, then relax on Playa Norte — consistently ranked among the most beautiful beaches in the world — with its calm, shallow, impossibly blue water.
day_by_day.evening: Return by catamaran to Cancun as the sun begins its descent. Freshen up at the resort and enjoy a quiet, elegant dinner at one of the Hotel Zone's finest establishments.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — light options such as yogurt parfait, fresh fruit, croissants, and espresso to fuel the morning adventure.
meals.lunch: Lunch on Isla Mujeres at Mango Café or Olivia Restaurant — savor fresh-caught fish, Mediterranean-inspired dishes, and tropical cocktails steps from Playa Norte.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Harry's Prime Steakhouse & Raw Bar (Cancun Hotel Zone) — a premier fine-dining destination known for USDA Prime dry-aged cuts, fresh oysters, and an award-winning wine list. Perfect for a luxurious evening after a full day at sea.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private catamaran charter at least 2–3 days in advance through the resort concierge. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a light cover-up, and a waterproof bag for valuables. The full Isla Mujeres day trip typically runs 9:00 AM–5:00 PM. Snorkeling equipment is usually provided on premium charters.

day_by_day.morning: Swim in the Cenotes at Dos Ojos — Embark on a private guided excursion to Dos Ojos, one of the world's most spectacular freshwater cave systems located near Cancun (approximately 1.5–2 hours south via private transfer). Snorkel or dive through otherworldly underground caverns illuminated by ethereal light filtering through the jungle canopy above.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cenote experience, stop at the nearby Riviera Maya town of Tulum for a curated lunch and a brief exploration of the clifftop Tulum archaeological ruins overlooking the Caribbean Sea — a breathtaking and exclusive afternoon detour.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun via private luxury vehicle. Arrive back at the resort in time for a relaxing swim or jacuzzi session before dinner. Enjoy a quieter, intimate evening at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before the excursion — fuel up with a hearty spread: huevos rancheros, fresh tropical fruit, whole-grain toast, and cold-brew coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Tulum at Hartwood or Gitano — two world-renowned open-air restaurants celebrated for their wood-fire cooking, farm-to-table ingredients, and jungle ambiance. Reserve well in advance.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant — enjoy a tasting menu with wine pairings, featuring contemporary Mexican cuisine crafted with locally sourced seafood and seasonal ingredients.

day_by_day.notes: Dos Ojos requires advance booking and a private round-trip transfer from Cancun. Wear a swimsuit under your clothes, bring water shoes, and avoid applying sunscreen or bug spray before entering the cenotes to protect the fragile ecosystem. The full day excursion including Tulum will run approximately 8:00 AM–7:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Playa Tortugas Beach Club Experience — Head to Playa Tortugas, one of the liveliest and most vibrant beaches in the Hotel Zone. Secure a premium daybed or cabana at one of the upscale beach clubs (such as Mandala Beach Club or Dady'O Beach). Enjoy watersports including jet skiing, paddleboarding, or parasailing over the turquoise Caribbean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your beach club experience through the early afternoon with cocktails, fresh seafood bites, and music. Later, return to the resort for a leisurely wind-down — perhaps a private yoga session on your balcony or a dip in the resort pool as the afternoon light softens.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your penultimate evening in Cancun with a special night out. Enjoy cocktails at a rooftop bar followed by a memorable fine-dining dinner at one of Cancun's most prestigious restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely late breakfast at the resort — smoked salmon eggs Benedict, fresh-squeezed juice, and a champagne mimosa to start the beach day right.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Playa Tortugas beach club — indulge in fresh ceviche, grilled lobster tacos, tropical fruit platters, and signature cocktails served directly to your cabana.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tempo by Heinz Beck (inside The Grand at Moon Palace or a comparable luxury venue) — a Michelin-starred chef's outpost offering Italian-Mediterranean haute cuisine with impeccable service and an extensive wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: Reserve your premium cabana or daybed at Playa Tortugas beach club at least one day in advance to guarantee the best spots. Most beach clubs have a minimum spend policy that is easily met with food and drinks. Bring cash or card for tips and any additional watersport rentals.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — Rise early for one last sunrise walk along the resort's private beach. Collect shells, take photos of the Caribbean at its most peaceful, and enjoy a slow, indulgent morning. Optional: book a final sunrise paddleboard session or a guided snorkeling excursion directly from the resort's beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort (standard checkout is typically 12:00 PM — request a late checkout if your flight allows). Enjoy one final swim in the pool or sea before your private luxury transfer to Cancun International Airport. Spend any remaining time browsing duty-free shops for premium tequila, artisan chocolates, or local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cancun. Reflect on an extraordinary six days of Caribbean luxury, world-class beaches, and unforgettable experiences.

meals.breakfast: A grand farewell breakfast at the resort — order the full à la carte menu and savor every last bite: fresh tropical fruits, Mexican-style chilaquiles, artisan pastries, and a celebratory glass of fresh-squeezed orange juice.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort's poolside bar or beachfront café — keep it simple with a shrimp ceviche, guacamole, and a final frozen margarita before heading to the airport.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining — if time permits before departure, enjoy a pre-flight meal at one of the premium airport lounges. Alternatively, the resort concierge can arrange a packed gourmet box for your journey home.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your checkout time and private airport transfer with the resort concierge the evening before. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the transfer and international check-in procedures. Consider purchasing premium Mexican tequila (such as Casa Dragones or Don Julio 1942) at the duty-free shops as a luxurious souvenir.
